answers.explanation: Four octets of 8 bits. (IPv6 addresses are 128 bits.)
8 + 2 = 10, so the 8 and 2 bits are on: 00001010.
Each octet is 8 bits, so it can only be 0 to 255. 300 doesn't fit.
All eight bits on: 128+64+32+16+8+4+2+1 = 255, the largest octet.
The network ID is shared; the host ID tells hosts on that network apart.
Forwarding tables list networks. That keeps them small enough to work at the scale of the Internet.
Clients come and go, so DHCP hands out addresses as needed. Servers need a stable address that others can find.
ipconfig on Windows, ifconfig on macOS, ip addr on Linux.
